job.title: People & Culture Adviser
job.description:
JOB TITLE: People & Culture Adviser

JOB LOCATION: 35 Collins Street, Melbourne/Hybrid


About the role

Reporting to the People Central Team Leader, the P&C Adviser is responsible for day-to-day maintenance and management of information in SAP SuccessFactors particularly in the Employee Central (EC) module and onboarding of new starters, ensuring all information is received to create a new employee profile.

The EC module contains information on position management, organisational structures, employee information and workflows related to approvals for actions by delegates in the system. As part of the People Central team, this role oversees the functions of the system for EC and onboarding, ensuring workflows reach the correct delegate, information is maintained accurately and actions relating to information flowing across the system are processed in a timely manner.

Key Accountabilities

  1. Ensure timely and accurate HR delegation, process and policy advice is provided to staff within the DGS cluster, using sound consultancy and negotiation skills to assist clients in clarifying needs, expectations and outcomes as well as providing advice in a timely manner. Ensure workflow management in SuccessFactors is in line with relevant departmental HR delegations.
  2. Provide advice and support on a broad range of HR system, position management and recruitment issues and practices, offering system solutions which are in line with organisational priorities and relevant government and department policy.
  3. Work with the People Central Service Delivery Manager and Team Leader to provide support and response to day-to-day HR questions and queries, using the Salesforce system to resolve tier 2 customer queries and tier 1 escalations.
  4. Support workforce planning and establishment management by maintaining and updating the organisational structure with SAP SuccessFactors (Employee Central).
  5. Escalate any SAP SuccessFactors system issues unable to be resolved by the P&C Service Delivery Team or tier 1 support teams.
  6. Prepare succinct and high-quality briefs, reports and other correspondence on a range of employment and workforce issues within tight timeframes.
  7. Support P&C projects and continuous improvement initiatives as required.

Key selection criteria

  1. Transactional Processing: exercises a high level of attention to detail when processing employee lifecycle changes, such as onboarding, transfers, and employee data changes, as well as the delivery of data entry and maintenance of organisational structure within the VicGov People system. 
  2. Communication: strong communication skills with both internal and external stakeholders; ability to tailor communications according to the audience and/or audience preference with the ability to influence and negotiate with stakeholders at varying levels. 
  3. Flexibility and adaptability: ability to take on a range of tasks and adjust approach and priorities to suit to changing requirements and the ability to multi-task and manage multiple priorities.
  4. Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: resolves issues through understanding and interpretation of existing processes and guidance, applying critical thinking and problem-solving concepts in the right context.
  5. Systems Thinking: understands system workflows and impacts of particular courses of action on other parts of the system, function or team more broadly.

Mandatory/desirable requirements

  1. Experience managing workflows within SAP SuccessFactors (Employee Central) is highly desirable.
  2. Experience with high volume processing of workflows, queries and requests. 
  3. Experience maintaining organisational establishments and position data within a HR information system. 
  4. Understanding of the legislative and industrial framework that applies to Victorian public servants, including the Public Administration Act 2004, the Fair Work Act 2009, Executive Handbook and the Victorian Public Service Enterprise Agreement 2024.
  5. Experience using Salesforce or a relevant service management tool to manage customer queries and requests

JOB TITLE: Workday Integration Support Lead

JOB LOCATION: Melbourne preferred; Sydney and Adelaide candidates also considered (Hybrid)

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Workday Integration Support Lead to own the operational stability, support, governance, and continuous improvement of integrations between Workday and enterprise platforms. The role will lead L2/L3 integration support, coordinate incident resolution, manage monitoring and release activities, and provide technical leadership across inbound and outbound interfaces. The successful candidate will work closely with Workday functional teams, security, reporting, infrastructure, middleware, third-party vendors, and business stakeholders to ensure integrations remain reliable, secure, supportable, and aligned with business priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Support Leadership

  • Lead day-to-day L2/L3 production support for Workday integrations, interfaces, and scheduled data transfers.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for high-priority incidents, recurring failures, and complex integration defects.
  • Triage incidents, determine business impact, coordinate resolver teams, and drive issues through to root-cause resolution.
  • Prioritise break-fix, service requests, minor enhancements, regulatory changes, and technical debt within the support backlog.
  • Coordinate with Workday functional leads to assess business-process, security, reporting, and configuration dependencies.
  • Provide clear stakeholder updates during incidents and escalate risks, constraints, and vendor dependencies when required.

Monitoring and Operational Control

  • Own integration monitoring, alerting, daily health checks, failure management, restart procedures, and operational dashboards.
  • Monitor scheduled and event-driven integrations, including inbound, outbound, file-based, API-based, and middleware-managed interfaces.
  • Ensure failures are identified promptly, data is reprocessed safely, and downstream impacts are assessed before closure.
  • Define support thresholds, alert routing, on-call or after-hours escalation requirements, and operational hand-offs.
  • Maintain integration inventories, schedules, dependencies, owners, service criticality, and support contacts.
  • Track availability, incident trends, repeat failures, ageing defects, and service performance for governance reporting.

Technical Troubleshooting and Development

  • Troubleshoot Workday integrations using integration event details, process monitor, audit information, reports, logs, and error outputs.
  • Support and enhance integrations built with Workday Studio, Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), Core Connectors, Cloud Connect, Report-as-a-Service (RaaS), Workday Web Services, REST/SOAP APIs, and custom reports.
  • Analyse and resolve issues involving XSLT, XML, JSON, CSV, web services, authentication, certificates, encryption, file transfer, data transformation, and sequencing.
  • Coordinate troubleshooting across middleware and external platforms, including SFTP endpoints, banking, payroll, procurement, asset-management, billing, HR, and identity systems.
  • Build or modify integration components where appropriate, following design, security, testing, and change-control standards.
  • Perform impact analysis before changes to Workday business processes, security, calculated fields, reports, endpoints, or external-system specifications.

Release, Change and Environment Management

  • Lead technical assessment and regression planning for Workday feature releases and integration-impacting changes.
  • Manage integration changes through development, test, deployment, and post-production validation in line with change-management controls.
  • Coordinate tenant refresh impacts, endpoint updates, credentials, certificates, schedules, and post-refresh validation.
  • Prepare deployment plans, backout plans, verification steps, implementation evidence, and change records.
  • Support cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition-to-support activities for new projects and interfaces.
  • Ensure separation of duties and appropriate approvals are maintained across build, migration, and production support.

Security, Compliance and Risk

  • Partner with Workday Security teams to maintain integration system users, integration security groups, domain permissions, authentication methods, and least-privilege access.
  • Monitor certificate, key, password, token, and endpoint expiry risks and coordinate timely renewals.
  • Ensure sensitive data is appropriately protected in transit and at rest, including secure file transfer, encryption, masking, and controlled logging.
  • Support audit requests by providing configuration, access, change, test, and operational evidence.
  • Maintain integration risks, known errors, control gaps, remediation actions, and continuity procedures.

Governance, Documentation and Continuous Improvement

  • Chair or contribute to integration support reviews, incident reviews, change forums, release planning, and service-governance meetings.
  • Own or maintain integration design documents, support guides, runbooks, monitoring procedures, data mappings, interface catalogues, and knowledge articles.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents and ensure preventative actions are implemented.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual intervention, improve observability, standardise patterns, and retire fragile interfaces.
  • Provide coaching, work allocation, technical review, and knowledge transfer for integration support consultants and partner resources.
  • Collaborate with implementation partners and vendors while retaining clear internal ownership of service outcomes.

  • 7+ years of Workday integration experience, including significant experience in production support or managed-service environments.
  • Hands-on expertise with Workday Studio, EIB, Core Connectors, RaaS, custom reports, calculated fields, Workday Web Services, and REST/SOAP APIs.
  • Strong troubleshooting capability across XML, XSLT, JSON, web services, SFTP, PGP encryption, certificates, authentication, and data transformation.

  • Working knowledge of Workday security concepts relevant to integrations, including integration system users, security groups, domains, and least-privilege access.
  • Experience with integration monitoring, operational dashboards, service reporting, root-cause analysis, and support documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

job.title: Manager, Water and Waste
job.description:
Lead essential services. Shape critical infrastructure. Make an impact you can see.

There are leadership roles where you maintain what already exists. Then there are opportunities to shape what comes next.

Davidson Executive & Talent is partnering with Cook Shire Council to appoint its next Manager Water and Waste, leading the essential water, wastewater and waste services that support communities across one of Queensland’s most unique regions.

Based in Cooktown and reporting to the Director Infrastructure, you’ll lead an experienced team of approximately 28 people across water, wastewater, waste and electrical maintenance. You’ll also oversee an operating budget of approximately $9.3 million across these essential services.

Your remit combines technical leadership with asset management, commercial thinking, regulatory compliance and long-term service planning.

The opportunity
This is a role for a leader who wants to build, improve and influence.

There is a significant infrastructure agenda ahead, including new and upgraded water and wastewater infrastructure in Lakeland and Coen, alongside the opportunity to strengthen asset management and shape a practical future waste strategy.

Your early priorities will be clear:

  • Strengthen regulatory and legislative compliance
  • Improve asset management and long-term infrastructure planning
  • Lead, mentor and get the best from an experienced, long-tenured team
  • Build robust business cases that connect infrastructure needs with funding and investment decisions
  • Bring a commercial lens to operational and capital planning
  • Manage and optimise a significant operating budget across water, wastewater and waste services
  • Work confidently with executives, councillors, regulators, contractors and communities

The role spans a large geographic footprint, so visible leadership matters. You’ll spend time with your people, understand the assets firsthand and be comfortable getting out across the region rather than leading solely from behind a desk.

The leader we’re looking for
Your strongest technical grounding will be in water and wastewater. You understand treatment, infrastructure, compliance and the consequences of getting essential services wrong.

You’ll also bring:

  • Leadership experience across water, wastewater and/or waste services
  • Strong asset lifecycle, renewal and capital planning capability
  • Commercial and financial acumen, including responsibility for significant operating budgets and business cases
  • Sound knowledge of relevant regulatory and environmental requirements
  • Experience leading people through change and improving established ways of working
  • The ability to turn complex technical issues into clear recommendations and gain stakeholder support
  • Strong judgement, communication and stakeholder management skills
  • Relevant engineering qualifications or extensive equivalent experience

You don’t necessarily need to come directly from local government. If you bring the technical credibility, commercial judgement and leadership capability, Council can support you in understanding its processes and environment.

Why Cooktown?
Cooktown may not have been where you expected your next career move to take you. That could be exactly what makes this opportunity worth exploring.

You’ll be joining a close-knit organisation with people who care deeply about their community. Council’s Director Infrastructure describes the management team as among the best they have worked with across their career in Australia and internationally, highlighting its integrity, low-ego approach and genuine commitment to community outcomes.

Cooktown offers a very different pace to metropolitan life, without being disconnected from the essentials. The region has schools, health services and airport access, with Cairns approximately a 45-minute flight away. Housing can be challenging, and Council can assist successful candidates in navigating local accommodation options.

We’ll be open about the move, the location and what the role involves. We want you to understand Cooktown properly and decide whether the opportunity is right for you.

Ready for something different?
If you’re an experienced water and wastewater leader looking for greater scope, visible impact and the opportunity to help shape essential infrastructure for the future, we’d like to start a conversation.

You don’t need to have made your mind up about Cooktown before you call.


For a confidential discussion, contact William Stock at Davidson Executive & Talent on william.stock@davidsonwp.com
